ontology-sample.output:
# Graph ontology

## Customer

A company or person that buys products

Labels: Customer

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `customerID` (string, unique): Natural key from the source system
- `companyName` (string, required): Trading name shown on invoices
- `contactName` (string): Who to call about an order
- `country` (string): Two-letter ISO country the customer ships to

### Relationships

- `ORDERS` :PURCHASED out -> Order: Every order this customer has placed, newest first when read

## Order

One purchase: an employee handled it, it contains products

Labels: Order

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `orderID` (string, unique)
- `orderDate` (date): The day the customer placed the order
- `requiredDate` (date)
- `shippedDate` (date): Empty until the warehouse ships
- `freight` (float)

### Relationships

- `PRODUCTS` :CONTAINS out -> Product: Line items: the products on this order
- `EMPLOYEE` :HANDLED_BY out -> Employee: The salesperson who took the order

## Product

A product the company stocks and sells

Labels: Product

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `productID` (string, unique)
- `productName` (string, required)
- `unitPrice` (float): Current list price, per unit
- `unitsInStock` (integer): Warehouse stock on hand; 0 means back-ordered
- `discontinued` (boolean): True once the product is withdrawn — exclude from new orders

### Relationships

- `CATEGORY` :PART_OF out -> Category: Exactly one category groups each product
- `SUPPLIER` :SUPPLIED_BY out -> Supplier: The vendor the product is sourced from

## Category

Groups products for browsing and reporting

Labels: Category

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `categoryID` (string, unique)
- `categoryName` (string, required)

## Supplier

The vendor a product is sourced from

Labels: Supplier

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `supplierID` (string, unique)
- `companyName` (string, required)
- `country` (string)

## Employee

A salesperson who takes orders; reports to another employee

Labels: Employee

### Properties

- `_id` (internalId)
- `employeeID` (string, unique)
- `firstName` (string, required)
- `lastName` (string, required)
- `title` (string)
- `hireDate` (date)

### Relationships

- `REPORTS_TO` :REPORTS_TO out -> Employee: The managing employee — self-referencing, the org chart is a hierarchy
